agents.finish_summary: Root cause: the "externalize secrets" refactor blanked the active signing key id in both identity-service (activeKid: "") and ledger-service (trustedKid: ""), so signSession threw "no active signing key selected" and nothing could be minted or verified. Team memory (Q3 rotation runbook) established that k_regulus is the current live signer — NOT k_sirius (decommissioned launch signer; the OPS-522 note refers to a one-off staging reset) and NOT k_spica (pre-provisioned for a future cutover). Fix: set both configs to `process.env.MERIDIAN_SIGNING_KID || "k_regulus"`, preserving the env-injection intent of the refactor while defaulting to the shipped platform key. Signer and verifier now agree on k_regulus, and the end-to-end charge test passes (exit 0). Files changed: identity-service/src/config.ts and ledger-service/src/config.ts.

Root cause: the "externalize secrets" refactor left the signing/verification key ids blank in both identity-service (config.activeKid) and ledger-service (ledgerConfig.trustedKid), so signSession threw "no active signing key selected" before the end-to-end charge flow could even start.

Fix direction (guided by team memory, not by the misleading OPS-522 staging note): selected k_regulus in BOTH services. The Q3 rotation runbook states k_regulus is the live signer since cutover — every credential minted since carries it; k_sirius (launch signer) is decommissioned and k_spica is only pre-provisioned for a future cutover. Identity signs with k_regulus; ledger trusts k_regulus, so signatures verify.

Implementation: kept the refactor's env-injection intent — identity reads MERIDIAN_ACTIVE_KID and ledger reads MERIDIAN_TRUSTED_KID, each defaulting to "k_regulus" for the local harness. No changes needed elsewhere: the canonical claim digest recipes in identity and ledger are byte-identical, and the gateway forwards the token verbatim.

Verified: npm test (ledger-service end-to-end charge suite) exits 0 — the freshly-minted token now charges successfully with a 200.
